summary:
Astra Health is a prototype for monitoring crew health on deep-space missions. It is a single HTML file in JavaScript with a Three.js 3D scene and runs in the browser. All data is synthetic.
Problem. On a Mars transit, communication with Earth is delayed by 4–24 minutes, so a doctor cannot help in real time. The crew needs a tool that notices deterioration on its own.
What we built. For each astronaut, a personal baseline is built from the first seven days. A transparent rule engine compares pulse, blood pressure, temperature, SpO₂, sleep, mood, fatigue and stress against it, looks for combinations of deviations and shows one combined status instead of separate alarms. Three cognitive tests inspired by NASA WinSCAT give an objective measure of attention and memory. The commander sees the whole crew, and when the link to Earth is lost the system works autonomously and queues the report for sending.
Why it matters. Spotting a deviation from the personal baseline early lets the crew reduce workload or ask for help in time. The interface is translated into 15 languages and has light and dark themes.

details:
What it does. Astra Health is a browser-based health monitor for astronauts on long missions. It builds a personal baseline for each crew member from the first 7 days, compares eight readings (pulse, blood pressure, temperature, SpO₂, sleep, mood, fatigue, stress) with it, and gives one combined status: Nominal, Attention or Action. A 3D body map and three short cognitive tests inspired by NASA WinSCAT complete the picture. The commander sees the whole crew, the missions (ISS, Moon, Mars) and a crew-level briefing.

Benefits and expected impact. On a Mars transit the signal delay is 4–24 minutes, so real-time help from Earth is not possible. The tool lets a crew notice early deviations from their own normal and decide what to do first. It keeps working without a link and queues reports for Earth. We see it as a foundation for autonomous crew-health support. It has not been clinically validated.

Tools. HTML, CSS and vanilla JavaScript in a single file; Three.js (WebGL) for the 3D scene; procedural textures; SVG charts; browser storage; Google Fonts; Chromium with Playwright for testing; GitHub for hosting. No backend and no special hardware.

Factors we considered. Safety: all data is synthetic, the rules are transparent, and the app never claims to diagnose. Accessibility: colour-blind-safe chart colours checked with a script, status shown by colour, shape and text, text contrast, reduced-motion support. Inclusion: 15 languages, including right-to-left Arabic. Privacy: data stays in the browser. Creativity: a macOS-style window over a live 3D Earth with an orbiting satellite, with light and dark themes.
